arcs.title: Dana and the basil cups
arcs.stage: 3/5 as planned — her Nov 5 promise to see Moshe could not be checked today (live log unreachable). Tonight Ishai tells Noa. Next: her visit, Saturday night Nov 7.

arcs.title: Saving Moshe
arcs.stage: 1/3 — Dry leaves, plucked by Ishai. Dana's house call is Saturday night.

arcs.title: Gadi and the chickpea logo
arcs.stage: Due Sunday morning. Today two pages of friendliness notes and no fee number yet; Noa pushes him to ask again on Sunday.

arcs.title: Noa, the best friend
arcs.stage: Today she apologises for Wednesday by phone and comes for Shabbat dinner, late, with wine.

arcs.title: Falafel the dog
arcs.stage: Settled in. Mrs. Levi objects to his nails and feeds him crusts.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 1 was planned for Nov 5 (not verified). Tonight he does the homework by accident: he doesn't say sorry back to Noa. Next: lesson 2, Thu Nov 12.

beats.goal: Friday morning at the desk with the chickpea logo, due Sunday morning. Gadi emails two pages of notes on friendliness. Ishai wants this done before Shabbat so he can have tonight and tomorrow free.
beats.forceText: Ishai works on the chickpea logo at his desk while Falafel sleeps at his feet. An email from Gadi lands.

forceLines.say: Two pages. On how friendly a chickpea should be.

forceCommentary.say: Two pages on one chickpea. Moshe got less attention than that.

moments.text: Ishai sits at the laptop with coffee, the chickpea logo filling the screen, Falafel asleep across his feet. An email arrives and he reads it twice.

message.say: Client's friendliness notes attached, two pages. Just one small thing: Sunday morning stands. Thanks in advance.

lines.say: Two pages. On how friendly a chickpea should be.

commentary.say: Two pages about a legume. Somewhere a novelist is jealous.
Thanks in advance. The rudest kind of thanks.

moments.text: He drags the chickpea's corners a little rounder, leans back, tilts his head, and looks down at the dog for a second opinion.

lines.say: Is that friendly, Falafel, or does it look like it wants something?

commentary.say: He's asking the dog. The dog has better taste than the client.

beats.goal: Ishai goes to Shuk Shalom for the Shabbat shopping before it closes at 14:00, with the Friday crowd around him. Noa phones about dinner tonight: she owes him for missing the cafe and the bar on Wednesday, she is bringing wine, and she wants to know what he is cooking.
beats.forceText: Ishai stands in the Friday crowd at Shuk Shalom with a full bag, the phone at his ear.

forceLines.say: Tonight. I'm bringing wine. What are you cooking?

forceCommentary.say: Noa on time for a phone call. Progress.

moments.text: The Friday crowd pushes between the stalls at Shuk Shalom. Ishai, a bag of vegetables on one arm, answers his phone with his shoulder.

lines.say: Ishush. Tell me there's food tonight, or I'm eating your plant.
I'm at the market right now. Chicken, potatoes, the good tomatoes.
Who taught you the good tomatoes?
Nobody. I squeezed a few and a man yelled at me.
That's how everyone learns. Listen, about Wednesday.
Which part of Wednesday?
Both parts. The cafe and the bar. I was a bad friend twice in one day.
You were. And I sat with Kobi for an hour.
So I'm bringing the good wine.
What time, in real time, not Noa time?

commentary.say: She apologised to him. On a Friday. Someone check the sky.
He squeezed tomatoes and got yelled at. Best customer service in the country.

moments.text: He pockets the phone and works his way down the row of stalls, adding bread and a bunch of parsley, checking the time before the stalls start closing.

lines.say: Six, she says. So, eight.

commentary.say: He has learned to convert Noa time. That is what friendship is.

beats.goal: Back home with the shopping, Ishai meets Mrs. Levi in the corridor. She has baked too much challah, as every Friday, and gives him one. She asks who is coming tonight and notices his bags. She complains about the dog's nails and sneaks Falafel something anyway.
beats.forceText: Mrs. Levi stops Ishai in the corridor and puts a warm challah on top of his shopping.

forceLines.say: Take it, motek. Who's it for tonight?
Noa's coming. Thank you, Mrs. Levi.

forceCommentary.say: Mrs. Levi runs the only intelligence agency funded by challah.

moments.text: Ishai comes up the stairs with his bags and Falafel at his heels. Mrs. Levi's door opens before he reaches his own, and a warm challah wrapped in a towel comes out first.

lines.say: Motek, stop. You look thin. Take this, I made too many.
Mrs. Levi, you make too many every week.
Every week there's somebody thin. Who's coming tonight?
Noa. My friend. You've seen her.
The one with the drawings on her arms, who runs on the stairs.
That's the one.
A good girl. Loud shoes. And this dog of yours, his nails on my floor.
I'll cut them after Shabbat, I promise.
Don't promise, cut. Here, for him, it's only a crust.
You said you don't like him.
I don't. Shabbat shalom, motek.

commentary.say: She hates the dog so much she feeds him by hand.
A challah handed over with a full background check.

moments.text: In the kitchen he unpacks, sets the challah on the counter under its towel, and starts on the chicken and potatoes, the radio low.

lines.say: Moshe, don't look. It's nothing personal, it's dinner.

commentary.say: He warned the basil before touching the chicken. A true gentleman.

beats.goal: Before sunset Ishai finishes cooking, puts the phone and laptop away and lights the Shabbat candles at home, alone with Falafel and Moshe. Quiet and warm.
beats.forceText: Ishai lights two candles on the table, covers his eyes for a moment, and the apartment goes quiet.

forceCommentary.say: No lines, no drama. I hate how much I like this.

moments.text: The food is done. Ishai closes the laptop on the chickpea, puts his phone in a drawer and sets the table for two, Mrs. Levi's challah in the middle.

lines.say: Chickpea, you've got until Saturday night. Rest.

commentary.say: He closed the laptop with Gadi still out there. Bravest thing all week.

moments.text: As the light outside turns orange he lights two candles, covers his eyes for a moment and says the blessing under his breath. Falafel watches the flames from the rug.

lines.say: Shabbat shalom, you two.

commentary.say: You two. A dog and a basil. I'm not crying, you are.

beats.goal: Shabbat dinner at home with Noa, who is late and brings wine. Real talk between old friends: she teases him about the improv lessons she paid for, about his fee with Gadi, and about the person coming to look at the basil tomorrow night. Yael's homework was to not say sorry to someone who should be saying it to him, and tonight he manages it, by accident, with her. Noa leaves by about 23:00.
beats.forceText: Ishai and Noa sit at the candle-lit table with Mrs. Levi's challah between them.

forceCommentary.say: He didn't say sorry back. Yael should get a raise.

moments.text: A knock, long after six. Noa comes in with a bottle of wine, kicks off her shoes and looks at the set table, the two candles and the dog.

lines.say: Shabbat shalom. Don't look at the clock.
I wasn't. I said six, you said six, it's almost eight.
The candles are still going. That's basically on time.
The chicken has a different opinion.
Is that Mrs. Levi's challah? She gave you one and you lived?
She gave the dog a crust and said she hates him.
So she's in love. Where's the opener?
Second drawer. Under the phone, don't touch the phone.
Look at you. A man with rules.
One rule. It's one night.

commentary.say: Two hours late and she's marking his attendance.
The chicken has an opinion. It's the only guest who was on time.

moments.text: They sit down at the table with the candles between them. Ishai says the blessing quickly over the wine and the challah and starts serving. Noa pauses with her fork in the air.

lines.say: This is good. Why is this good?
I had time to worry about it.
So tell me about Yael. How much do you hate me?
She stops me with one clap. I hear it in my sleep.
Did you ask for a refund yet?
She already knew I would. You warned her.
I did. Listen, the chicken was cold because of me. I'm sorry.
It's okay, I should have... No. Wait. Say that again.
What?
The part where you're sorry. I'm not saying it back.
Who are you, and what have you done with Ishush?
That was my homework.

commentary.say: He held a whole silence. Somewhere, one clap.
Noa is speechless. Frame this. Hang it in the bar.

moments.text: Later, plates pushed aside and the candles lower, they sit with what's left of the wine. Noa wanders to the windowsill and turns Moshe's pot to get a look at him.

lines.say: He looks like a man who got bad news.
He's resting. Someone's coming tomorrow night to look at him.
Someone.
Dana. From the cafe. She knows about plants.
The barista is making a house call for a basil.
It's a plant visit. It's agricultural.
Ishush. Are you cleaning the apartment for this agricultural visit?
A little.
And the fee? Did Gadi give you a number?
He gave me two pages of friendliness.
So that's a no. Sunday you ask again, with your new spine.

commentary.say: Agricultural! Tomorrow night. I have never been more ready for a plant.
Moshe is being used as an excuse. He deserves an agent.
